title: THE MYTH
sub: One narrative from every lab film, told by the archive films they keep returning to.

reel.line: First, they promised a future. In 1956, someone made a film called Spider Engineers. The spider is shown to be an engineer of great skill and versatility.
In Where You Go When You Leave, it played this: Bands diverge; home splits; eleven petals.

In 1950, the United States government made a film called Oil Across Arabia. It documents the early development of Saudi Arabia’s oil fields and construction of the Trans-Arabian Pipeline from Abqaiq to Sidon, Lebanon.
In our Odyssey, it was cast as extreme wide from the sea, crowds and smoking fires along a beach.

In 1950, California Packing Corporation (Del Monte) made a film called Golden Harvest...Fifty Years of Calpak Progress. History of a company involved in the California canning industry, with excellent footage of agribusiness and cannery operations dating back to the turn of the century.
In our Odyssey, it was cast as wide with ship whole and one man on a raft superimposed.
Then they explained how to live in it. In 1959, Encyclopaedia Britannica Films made a film called The Unique Contribution. How educational films contribute to teaching and learning.
In the Republic, it stood for the ground: red desert with rocks under a hazy sky.
In 1949, Centron Corporation made a film called Speech: Platform Posture and Appearance. Audiences are impressed by what they see as well as what they hear.
In our Odyssey, it was cast as push into the beautiful woman's face, gazing at the youth.
In 1950, Coronet made a film called The Fun That Builds Good Health. Presents a variety of choices of recreation in terms of good times and good health.
In our Odyssey, it was cast as four defenders throwing spears together, attackers falling.
And they sold it. In 1960, Consumers Union of the United States made a film called Consumers Want to Know. Inside the testing labs of Consumers Union, publisher of Consumer Reports.
In our Odyssey, it was cast as elder stepping back, arms folded, watching the fight.
In 1948, Chevrolet Division, General Motors Corporation made a film called The Things People Want. Distinctive sales training film on the hierarchy of human needs, starring a young John Forsythe.
Aurora made a film called Aurora Stunt and Drag Race Set Commercial. Television commercial for Aurora Stunt and Drag Race toy cars.
In our Odyssey, it was cast as hands lifting a long bow from a peg into a shaft of light.

But the future came with a warning. In 1992, the Department of Education made a film called Straight Talk. The documentary profiles four young people who explain why they won't use drugs and the techniques they use to stay drug free.
In Where You Go When You Leave, it played this: Street becomes living room; breakup remains.
In 1951, Frith Films made a film called Fire! Patty Learns What to Do. Fire safety film filmed in and around the Chatsworth fire of 1947 in the San Fernando Valley of Los Angeles.
In our Odyssey, it was cast as Boy working in a farmyard among adults.

Someone made a film called Safety: Harm Hides at Home. Uses a story about children who are rescued from accidents at home to create an awareness of home safety and provides examples for accident prevention.
In the Republic, it stood for a hand on a door handle.

So people went into the dark, and dreamed. In 1949, someone made a film called The Green Promise. Walter Brennan plays the part of a father raising four children, but has his own ideas about how to run a farm.
In Where You Go When You Leave, it played this: Thunderstorm consumes the chapel.
Someone made a film called Berlin: Symphony of a Great City. A classic silent film dedicated to Berlin shot in 1927 by Walter Ruttmann.
In our Odyssey, it was cast as long smoky hall, men feasting and gambling, a boy small at far end.

In 1935, Twickenham Film Studios made a film called Scrooge. Scrooge, the ultimate Victorian miser, hasn't a good word for Christmas, though his impoverished clerk Cratchit and nephew Fred are full of holiday spirit.
In our Odyssey, it was cast as bearded elder points, young man in winged cap bows.

And then ordinary people turned the camera on themselves. In 1938, Ivan Besse filmed his town: Britton, South Dakota. Daily life in a South Dakota town during the Great Depression, shot by Ivan Besse.
In Where You Go When You Leave, it played this: Mother and Poet watch Poet and Ex break up.
In 2007, Darrell Lee Wright made a film called Ripley's Believe it or Not Museum - Gatlinburg, Tennessee. Step inside the Gatlinburg, Tennessee Ripley's Believe it or Not Museum...IF YOU DARE!
In our Odyssey, it was cast as enormous one-eyed face bending into firelight.
In 2006, Belmont Historical Society made a film called Richard Betts Remembers. Town historian Richard Betts is interveiwed by Viktoria Haase on 01/05/06.
In Where You Go When You Leave, it played this: Photographs, film and fiction as memory inserts.
These films were made to explain the future. We made them play gods, settlers and ghosts. The people in them are still talking.
